text.reasoning: Five links from an open page to a ship the pilot is actually flying: a world, a ship in it, a clock, controls that answer, and a viewpoint. Each is the precondition of the next, so nothing here is reorderable.

nodes.name: The page builds a world to fly in

attrs.story: Opening the page constructs a WebGL renderer and a scene. Until this exists there is no space, no ship, nothing to look at.
acceptance: with WebGL unavailable the page reports it rather than showing a blank canvas
the renderer is constructed exactly once per page load

nodes.name: The game gives the pilot a ship

attrs.story: A ship is built for the player and placed in the world with a hull, a texture and a collision radius.
acceptance: ships[0] exists with role 'player' after load
the ship has a non-zero collision radius, so it can be hit

nodes.name: The simulation advances every frame

attrs.story: A frame loop runs, clamps the timestep so a stalled tab cannot teleport the world, and steps the simulation.
acceptance: a frame gap longer than 50ms is clamped rather than integrated whole
pausing and resuming the tab does not move the ship

nodes.name: The pilot's controls move the ship

attrs.story: Thrust, yaw and pitch answer the keyboard, bounded by drag and a maximum speed, so the ship is flyable rather than merely present.
acceptance: holding thrust raises speed until it plateaus at VMAX, not beyond
releasing thrust decays speed rather than stopping dead

nodes.name: The pilot can see where the ship is going

attrs.story: A chase camera trails the ship, leads it slightly, and lags rather than snapping, so the pilot has a usable frame of reference.
acceptance: the camera sits behind and above the ship at rest
a hard turn moves the camera smoothly, with no instantaneous jump

nodes.name: the simulation is stepping
the controls answer the pilot

text.reasoning: The epic's own sentence, one beat per clause: a field exists, you can find a rock in it, you break it, it leaves gems, you scoop them, the bar banks a point. The two system-side beats are in the chain because without them the pilot-side beats have nothing to act on.

nodes.name: The system populates a belt with rocks

attrs.story: A mining belt is seeded with instanced asteroids, capped so the field is dense without becoming thousands of draw calls.
acceptance: the field holds rocks up to AST_MAX and never more
rocks are drawn from instanced pools, not one mesh each

nodes.name: The system finds the rocks near the pilot cheaply

attrs.story: A spatial hash rebuilt every few frames answers 'what is near me' without scanning the field, which is what makes a belt of thousands testable every frame.
acceptance: collision testing does not scan every rock each frame
a rock marked gone is skipped by the near-query rather than returned

nodes.name: The pilot breaks a rock apart

attrs.story: A rock that takes enough damage is destroyed, splitting into smaller children carrying a fraction of its size and a kick outward.
acceptance: a destroyed rock above the no-split size yields between AST_SPLIT_MIN and AST_SPLIT_MAX children
the children move apart rather than sitting inside each other

nodes.name: Broken rock leaves gems in the world

attrs.story: The pieces spawn as physical gem pickups whose credit value scales with the size of the rock they came from, and which expire if nobody takes them.
acceptance: a bigger rock yields gems worth more credits than a smaller one
an uncollected gem disappears after GEM_LIFE seconds

nodes.name: The pilot scoops a gem

attrs.story: Flying near a gem collects it, with a magnet radius that widens as the ship is upgraded, so collection is a flight skill rather than a pixel-hunt.
acceptance: a gem inside the magnet radius moves toward the ship without an exact pass-over
the magnet radius grows when the relevant upgrade is bought

nodes.name: Collected credits bank an upgrade point

attrs.story: Gem credits fill a bar; each time it fills it converts into one banked upgrade point, up to a cap.
acceptance: GEM_BAR_MAX credits collected converts to exactly one banked point
only the player's ship banks points; an AI ship collecting gems banks none
banked points stop accumulating at GEM_PTS_CAP

nodes.name: a belt of rocks exists
a rock is within reach
gems are loose in the world
a gem can be picked up
gem credits are in the hold

text.reasoning: The decision the epic describes has two arms off one point: spend it now and get stronger immediately, or bank toward a maxed ship and trade the whole thing in. Both arms are in the chain, because the choice only exists if both are reachable.

nodes.name: The pilot spends a point on one of eight stats

attrs.story: A banked point goes into one of eight named stats, in flight, each capped so no single stat absorbs the whole run.
acceptance: spending on an unknown stat name is refused with the list of real ones
a stat already at STAT_MAX refuses further points rather than consuming them

nodes.name: Each point visibly changes how the ship performs

attrs.story: A stat is a multiplier the simulation actually reads, so a point spent is felt rather than merely displayed.
acceptance: raising speed increases the ship's achieved velocity in flight
a stat at zero leaves its multiplier at exactly 1.0

nodes.name: Maxing every stat arms the trade-in

attrs.story: Only when all eight stats are at their cap, with a further point banked, does the ship become eligible for the next hull.
acceptance: with seven stats maxed the tier-up is not offered
with eight maxed and no banked point the tier-up is not offered

nodes.name: The game names the hull that comes next

attrs.story: The ladder of hulls is a fixed order, and the ship's current class determines exactly which one is on offer.
acceptance: a ship at the top of the ladder is offered nothing
a generated hull is placed at its size tier's rank rather than off the ladder

nodes.name: Taking the new hull costs every upgrade bought

attrs.story: Accepting the trade-in swaps the frame and resets all eight stats to zero, which is what makes holding out a real decision rather than a free reward.
acceptance: after a tier-up every stat reads zero
refusing the tier-up leaves the current hull and stats untouched

nodes.name: at least one stat is above zero
every stat is at its cap
a next hull is on offer
the ship is flying a new frame

text.reasoning: The fight as a cost chain: firing costs energy, shots cost range, hits cost shields, exhausted shields cost the hull, the hull costs the cargo, and the cargo costs the run. Each beat is the precondition of the next loss.

nodes.name: Firing costs energy the pilot cannot spend forever

attrs.story: Each shot draws from a capacitor that refills over time, so sustained fire is bounded by a resource rather than by a cooldown alone.
acceptance: with the capacitor empty the ship cannot fire
breaking off refills the capacitor at LASER_CAP_REGEN per second
raising energyCap raises the ceiling the capacitor refills to

nodes.name: The pilot's shots reach and hurt what they hit

attrs.story: Bullets travel at a finite speed for a finite life and deal damage on contact, so range and lead are real constraints.
acceptance: a bullet expires after BULLET_LIFE seconds rather than travelling forever
firing faster than FIRE_CD apart is refused

nodes.name: Shields take the hit before the hull does

attrs.story: Damage is absorbed by a directional shield arc, each arc carrying half the ship's total shield, before any of it reaches the hull.
acceptance: a hit from ahead drains the forward arc and leaves the aft arc untouched
hull integrity does not fall while the struck arc still has charge

nodes.name: A ship that runs out of hull dies

attrs.story: When damage exhausts the hull the ship is destroyed and removed from the fight, with the kill attributed.
acceptance: a destroyed ship stops being a valid target
the killer is credited, so a kill is attributable

nodes.name: Death spills the cargo for anyone to take

attrs.story: The credits banked into the hold are dropped into the world on death, so a long uninterrupted run is worth more than the sum of its minutes.
acceptance: a pilot dying with credits leaves collectable gems at the wreck
a pilot dying with nothing spills nothing

nodes.name: The pilot comes back small after a pause

attrs.story: After a delay the pilot respawns without the hull they lost, which is the cost that makes the fight matter.
acceptance: respawn does not happen before RESPAWN_DELAY seconds have passed
the respawned ship is not the tier that died

nodes.name: the ship can fire
shots are being exchanged
a shield arc is down
the pilot's ship is destroyed
the hold is on the floor

text.reasoning: Persistence as a chain rather than a feature list: gather, write, keep current, restore, score. The cadence beat sits between writing and restoring because a save written only at the end does not survive the way a session actually ends.

nodes.name: The game gathers what is worth keeping

attrs.story: The player's ship, progress and standing are collected into one versioned snapshot.
acceptance: the snapshot carries a version field, so an old save is recognisable as old
with no player ship the snapshot is refused rather than written empty

nodes.name: The snapshot is written where it can be found again

attrs.story: The snapshot is stored under a known key in browser storage, so it survives the page closing.
acceptance: closing and reopening the page finds the previous snapshot
a snapshot written under the key replaces the previous one rather than accumulating

nodes.name: The snapshot is kept current, not written only at the end

attrs.story: Saving runs on a cadence during play, so an unclean exit costs at most one interval rather than the whole session.
acceptance: a session ended without a clean exit still restores to within SAVE_INTERVAL_S of where it stopped

nodes.name: A returning pilot gets their ship back

attrs.story: On load a valid snapshot of the right version is applied; an invalid or older one is declined rather than half-applied.
acceptance: a snapshot of the wrong version is declined and the pilot starts fresh
a restored pilot has the hull and stats they had when the snapshot was taken

nodes.name: The run's standing is a weighted total

attrs.story: Standing combines credits and score under a stated weight rather than counting kills alone, so mining and fighting both register.
acceptance: a run that only mines still produces a non-zero standing
two runs with equal credits and different scores are ranked apart

nodes.name: a snapshot of the run exists
the snapshot is in storage
the stored snapshot is no more than one interval old
a returning pilot has their ship back
